But whether those are materials that my working group processed or not, I can't say, because I can't see what is inside the box. I told you that I do not recognise this box. This is not one of the binders where I kept my materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you aware of the existence of any other bodies in the Ministry of Interior that was collecting evidence on military crimes at that time?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the working groups, I know that there was a group that I was a part of. The one established before me and where I joined. I know that the analytical processing of the materials went through the sector for analytics where Mrs. Katica Jovanovska was. The forensic processing went through the police forensics department where other colleagues were working, if that is what you are asking me about. And whether there were -- oh, I know that my colleagues in Kumanovo were working who used the same or similar methods as us in processing some of the cases that took place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Actually, I think my question was something a little different, Mr. Stojkov. You've read a label on a box which appears to refer to this box containing evidence material for military crimes, but you're saying you can't say that this -- this box contains material that your working group collected. What I'm saying is: Are you aware that any other working groups had been established doing the same work that you were?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time when I was an active member, when my working group was operating, I don't know whether there were any other working groups collecting materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if we could just move on perhaps to the next document, the next photograph, and this has the ERN N005-8228. And, Mr. Stojkov, I believe you said before that you recognised these folders or binders also. What do you recognise them to be?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one, at the front has my handwriting on the label. That belonged to my working group. Regarding the second one, I'm not sure. I can't really see it. I think that the title "Kumanovo" might be written by me, while the inscription above it is not in my handwriting. I'm not sure. But "Kumanovo" might be written by me. I'm sure that the inscription above is not written by me. Maybe it was written by another member of the group. With regards to the third binder, I can't read it. The photograph is poor, so I can't really say whether it was one of the -- the ones where I wrote the label or not. It is really illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Can I just ask you that folders or binders in which you wrote the label, did those binders contain documents from your working group?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period when I was working and when we handed over and when we kept the documents, they were here. I need to say again. What I say here is a binder. It has a label where the inscription is in my handwriting, but I can't say whether the materials inside are the materials from my working group or materials that I had processed or not. I could say that they might be inside or they might not be inside, because I don't see what is inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would seek to tender this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P563, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Am I right, you've not tendered the second of the three.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: No, I haven't, Your Honour, in light of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you're not wanting it marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't know whether I've confused the registry officer there.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The second photograph bearing ERN N005-8224 will be Exhibit P564, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, obviously, Mr. Stojkov, as you've testified, the working group had collected a significant amount of materials and these are boxes and folders demonstrate that, at least in this place, there were a significant number of materials also. If it were to be put to a witness before this Tribunal and that witness were agree that upon the change of government in Macedonia in 2001, the documents collected by the working group and the military crimes had been destroyed, from what we can see in these photographs that proposition would clearly be incorrect. Wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, as I stated already, you have here one part of the binders and folders containing some materials. I don't know what materials are inside. I can only make a conjecture that it is my materials inside. But certainly not everything is here. You have here three binders only. In my opinion there should be at least ten binders and ten boxes, and I can't even say whether the materials inside are my materials. Whether the materials after the change of government in 2002 and -- yes, towards the end of 2002, whether someone else, some other colleagues who came to work here, whether they destroyed the materials or not, I can tell you that I have heard many different versions, many versions were in circulation in the -- in the Ministry of Interior that some of the materials had disappeared, that some were hidden. But I never had any possibility or any competence to verify this. At the moment when we handed over the materials when actually our work was terminated and we were ordered to hand over the materials, from that moment onwards until the present day, I have not seen the materials; so I can't confirm either way, whether it was destroyed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, what you have seen in front of you, Mr. Stojkov, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies for interrupting my learned colleague in his cross-examination, but I think that the witness is being misled about the change of government in 2001. In 2001, there was no change of government, and this question misleads the witness. Perhaps it is only an error in the year, on the part of my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry. There was certainly no intent to mislead, and I believe the word I'd said was "after 2001." Perhaps I could have been more precise in stating the year, but there was no intention to mislead there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkov, if you put aside the possibility that someone has taken the boxes and binders that you prepared and wrote labels on, and put other documents inside, would you agree that there do appear to be documents from your working group still existing today?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All materials which we processed prior to the disbanding of the working group and which we submitted to the analytics department, this is where they should be. They're processed in the analytics department and then they're kept at the archives of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, you had mentioned earlier in response to a question of mine that you had heard rumours about material being hidden or possibly being destroyed. Was there an investigation into any of these rumours?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that these were rumours only. My position at the ministry, then and now, which has not changed, and this can be -- seen that I was an independent inspector at the unit for illicit drug trade and I'm still in the same position. From that position I could not confirm whether these rumours were correct or not or whether someone had undertaken measures to destroy or not destroy to hide or to take this material from the ministry. This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: My question is a little different. I'm asking if you know if there was any investigation into these rumours?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, I see that my colleague is on his feet, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies again for interrupting my learned colleague in his cross-examination. I was expecting him to ask the witness or at least our colleagues to tell us when these photographs were taken before continuing with his examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that something you're proposing, Mr. Dobbyn?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'm certainly happy to offer that information, Your Honour, and these photographs were taken last month, in the archives of the Ministry of Interior in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, if we can just go back to my question, Mr. Stojkov, which was did you have any knowledge as to whether there was any investigation into these rumours of missing files?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'd like to move on and perhaps look at some of the cases that were investigated by the working group into military or war crimes. And if we could turn to tab 5, and this is 65 ter number 1084. And if we could go to the first page, N006-7652. We appear to have the wrong document on e-court there. It's 65 ter 1084. Thank you. What we see here, Mr. Stojkov, is a document headed: File for the person Krstevski Borce. And it says: "Kidnapped and psycho-physically maltreated by the Albanian terrorists." Mr. Stojkov, are you able to recognise this as the cover page of -- of a file from your working group?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the file but it is not very well placed to name this person because he is still living in Macedonia. And since nothing has been undertaken until now by the bodies in Macedonia or by international bodies about the suffering of these people, I believe it is not well placed to show these people and to name them. Otherwise, I recognise this file, the first page, the cover page has been prepared by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of that, I would just ask that these not be published to the outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. That will be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could turn now to page N006-7658.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this should be approximately the seventh page in front of you, Mr. Stojkov, and the sixth page in English. And it will be a document entitled: Official Note number 2094. Do you have that document in front of you, Mr. Stojkov.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that this says: "MOI of the RM, UVR Tetovo, police station Tetovo," and it's dated 6th, 7th 2001. And the subject is: "Missing person reported." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And turning to the second paragraph you see that it states -- sorry, just to summarize, can you see from reading the paragraph that someone is reporting that his son went missing on the 5th of July, 2001. Do you follow that, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And I'd like to go to a different page now and I'm sorry if we're jumping backwards and forwards but these documents were not in chronological order whereas I would like to follow the chronological order. So if we could go back to the third page in the Macedonian and it's the second page in English. And the ERN is N006-7654 and it's an Official Note which is not numbered. Do you have that page in front of you, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see that this is an Official Note of an official interview conducted with an individual who was kidnapped and maltreated by the Albanian terrorists. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see at the start of the first paragraph that this interview was conducted on the 6th of September, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And from the top of the page, we can see that this Official Note was drafted sometime in 2002. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there is no date, I can presume that it's technical mistake because the interview was conducted on 6th of September, 2001. The place is listed where this interview was carried out, that this was not carried out in the official premises of police bodies. Therefore I can presume that it is a technical mistake of the date when the interview was carried out. In the upper part where the number and the date should be stated, it's -- this is left empty. This is left open so as when this document goes into the analytics sector, it is processed and listed under a number when it was processed. The text, on the other hand, explains exactly the den and the date when this happened and how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you see that the page in Macedonian, it has already typed, already included in the -- in the note the date 2002. So, clearly, some sort of processing took place in 2002 of this note. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean the date was erased? The date was never put in there. There's no date here. It's just 2002. That's put in the upper left corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojkov. That's exactly what I'm saying. It states 2002 in that document, doesn't it? So I'm saying that obviously there was some processing of this document that took place in 2002. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this document, according my modest police knowledge, has not been processed because it does not contain the number or a date when it was processed. It should have a register number under which all documents are entered, and then the date is written when they're processed. If you visited the Ministry of the Interior, the analytical department, someone should have informed you of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we'll move on from that point, Mr. Stojkov. If you look at the second paragraph on that page, do you see that this interview is in reference to something that happened on the night between the 3rd and 4rd of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is so stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in the last paragraph of that page it states: "There were four individuals dressed in camouflage uniforms with UCK emblems ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree that this document, running to four pages, appears to a lengthy and very comprehensive note of the contents of the interview which took place?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to read this text, from what I can see now, there's a chronological overview of what happened, what happened to that person from the moment he was kidnapped to the time when he was set free. Surely it includes a lot of information to that end. I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you go right to the end of the document, which is ERN N006-7657, do you see at the bottom, it says: "Submitted by," and it has the name Stojkov Igno. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to me, here we have my colleagues also who worked on this, which means that the three of us attended this interview and took part in this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall this specific interview?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I am able to see now, I can see that the interview was conducted in a student's home where misplaced persons were settled. This is where the interview was carried out and this person told us what had happened to him. Prior to this interview, there were also other conversations also. At first this person did not want to accept to tell us what had happened. He refused to cooperate with us at first, because he was not sure whether this will be material that will be kept over in the -- only in the ministry. People were afraid to talk about things like this. And this is a problem we encountered with everyone, with Macedonians, Albanians, Roma also, because this home had people from all ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkov, do you recall if you took the notes of this interview yourself?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps in my log I took notes, surely I must have taken notes. And most probably I might still have them, containing information about this person, perhaps the dates also when these things happened, and approximately what persons took part in this. But after such a long period of time, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: That's understandable, Mr. Stojkov. Perhaps if we can move on to what is page 10 in the Macedonian version, the ERN of this page is N006-7661. And it will have the title: "Record for admitting a criminal charge." Do you see this, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at the top it states: "Ministry of Interior; 28.3.2002; Record for admitting a criminal charge"; has the name of a reporting person. And it states that this file -- "this is a file of a criminal charge against an unknown committer for the criminal act of kidnapping and seizure of a private motor vehicle." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at the bottom do you see the official stamp of the Ministry of Interior, SVR Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And who would this record for admitting a criminal charge go to, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This record is submitted to the OVR in Tetovo. The person reported that in this period of time, was kidnapped, maltreated and then set free.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And when the OVR in Tetovo received this document, did they forward it on from there?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is kind of a specific document. It's dated 28 March, while we must have had this in copy from OVR Tetovo, since it exists in our file. The undersigned, we have who made the complaint, there were official persons involved, all of these persons have signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And does this document go to the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not tell you this. All of these documents, including this one, if it's in the file, has been processed to the analytics units. But whether they forward it to the basic public prosecutor's office or not, it's not something I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So this document is a complaint by a citizen, is that correct, or is it a charge forwarded by the police?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a form that is filled out by a person, injured person, coming to the police station wanting to submit a complaint. It could be this person or someone from his family. In the case that they want to report an event, whether it be a crime or an other kind of event the duty officer or the reception officer takes this information and makes a record of this in seven copies. There are seven such forms that include the basic information about the complainant. This is one such form, where the time, the manner, and the place of the event has taken place. All of these information given by the aggrieved person is entered by the duty officer or the reception officer, and is signed, you see down here below, three signatures. And this is prepared in seven copies. When one comes to a police station to report something, a form of this kind is filled for -- for preparing a criminal charge. Therefore, this is not a criminal charge.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: A criminal report, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you could move on to page N006-7666 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we move, would it be convenient to have a break at this time, Mr. Dobbyn?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe -- if we could allow another five minutes, we could finish with this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry. Before moving on quickly, could you explain, Mr. Stojkov, the seven copies that are prepared, what happens to those?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are processed. If the perpetrators of the crime are found, by rule, the criminal report is also prepared in several copies depending on the number of perpetrators, and depending on the type of crime but usually or, in the least, three copies are made which are part of the criminal report. One of them is written in hand, while the other three, one remains in the police station in the file of the responsible police officers, the other one goes to the unit of analytics of the police station and the other in the analytics of the Ministry of Interior or OVR -- SVR Skopje, if this was committed in Skopje. However, I am not an analyst and I cannot tell you in concrete terms. This is something that I have learned from my practice, because I have encountered forms of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would just like to be clear on this point, Mr. Stojkov. At least in the transcript you referred to seven copies. You have said that you have referred to -- you described what happens to three copies. What happens to the other four?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I explained this. If the alleged perpetrator is caught or the accused for the crime that has been reported, the form must be included in the criminal report which, through the analytics sector, it is then submitted to the public prosecutor's office. Depending on the crime and depending on the number of perpetrators, so many forms are prepared. If the perpetrators are not caught, if a report is not made, then this remains with the police officer or in the analytics sector. I'm not an analyst, I don't know. But I do know that one copy is kept with the responsible police officers so that he could work with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps this will be the last question we will ask on this for the moment. When the police receive a criminal charge like this against an unknown committer, will they then try to identify that unknown perpetrator and arrest that person?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a legal obligation and duty of police officers upon receipt of any report of an injured party to undertake measures and activities according to responsibilities and obligations to discover the perpetrator of this act. Therefore, measures have to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I think this might be an appropriate time to take a break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, CLSS reacted swiftly to our discussion regarding the translation and informed us during the break that the proper term for "voeni zlostorstva" is "war crimes," and at the same time, submitted corrected translation of our Exhibit 1D115. During the break, we submitted to the Prosecutor the original and the corrected document with the corrections from the CLSS. So I would like to hand out the corrections and allow us to replace the existing document, the original document, to replace it by the corrected translation from the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We have also seen the e-mail from CLSS and we're happy to accept that translation. Obviously, I'm working from some documents which -- they're draft translations and I will try to use the correct term; but if I slip, then I'm happy to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojkov, before we broke we had pulled up a page from the file that we had been examining and this is the page with ERN N006-7666. Do you have that page in front of you? It consists of some medical records.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you can see that these records come from the public health organisation clinic in Skopje and they relate to the person that this file is about. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So when investigating this case, at least, the working group was able to obtain medical records. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received the medical files from the persons that accepted to talk to us, to cooperate with the working group. I think that during my work, I'm speaking about myself only, I have not taken any medical documents from any health organisation in Skopje or elsewhere, unless they were brought by the aggrieved persons themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could go on to page N006-7672. And this should be the second-to-last page in the Macedonian version, Mr. Stojkov. And it's the last page of the English translations. Do you have that page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see that this document comes from the general city hospital in Skopje. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This document comes -- yes. Yes, the city General Hospital in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see the date, 18 December 2002?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: 18th or the 13th, I'm not sure, but it is December 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. So this clearly shows, doesn't it, that the working group was still gathering documents in relation to this case, at least until towards the end of 2002?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see, there is an addition from the 16th of February, 2002, on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And -- sorry, one moment there. Just to clarify what's on the record, you do agree that the date at the top of the page is either the 18th or the 13th of December, 2002. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is written here. I haven't issued this document, and I haven't signed it and I do not understand what is written in the document because this is a medical document. I have no medical skills, so I can't really say. But on the top of the page it is written 13th or the 18th of December, 2002. If this is what is written, it is possible that that was the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Stojkov, are you aware of the date that the amnesty law was passed in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but of course, the general public, the media published that the Law on Amnesty entered into force. I might have seen the document in some of the media, but I haven't had the opportunity to review it, but I knew that at one point the Law on Amnesty entered into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps could you turn to tab 15 in your binder, and this is Exhibit P00083. This is in tab 15, Mr. Stojkov. Do you have that? And if you look at the first page, do you see at the top it states: "Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, number 18, Friday, 8 March, 2002." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: March 7, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, if you go further above that, do you see the -- at the top of the page: "Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, number 18, Friday, 8 March 2002." Do you see that now?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper part, it is only written on the basis of Article 75, that is the first line of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, I see that myself. So we see the date, 7th March 2002, the heading under that decree for proclaiming the Law on Amnesty. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So would you agree that the Law on Amnesty was passed in early March 2002?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the Law on Amnesty obviously didn't put a halt to the working group's investigations into war crimes.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The working group on war crimes - I apologise - was working based on tasks given by our superior officer. At any moment when we have been told that the working group's activities terminate, we would have terminated them, but this Law on Amnesty applies to persons who perpetrated criminal offences during the armed conflict in the Republic of Macedonia. But this Law does not relieve of responsibility persons who had perpetrated grave offences against the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia. So the law cannot absolve someone who has perpetrated a murder. Do you agree, Mr. Prosecutor, with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojkov, I do apologise, but in the Tribunal here I am the one who asks the questions and I would ask you to answer them rather than the other way around. And my question, Mr. Stojkov, is did you receive any instructions to stop your investigations after the Law on Amnesty was passed in early March 2002?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not receive any instructions to stop the working of our working group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could move to tab 6, Mr. Stojkov, and here we'll see another file from the records of the working group, and this is 65 ter number 1091. And, Mr. Stojkov, if you look at the first page you'll see the heading: "File," has the name of a person. And it states: "Kidnapped and psycho-physically maltreated by the Albanian terrorists." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is this another file from the working group that you were a member of?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to -- like you to turn to the last page in this file, and the ERN is N006-7736. And this is an unnumbered Official Note, dated 29.6.2001. Do you see that document? This should be the last page. And, again, Mr. Stojkov, do you see that this document is dated 29 June 2001?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you can see from the subject that it's a report of a missing person. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report on missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we can turn back, please, to the fifth page in the Macedonian, it's the fourth page in English, the ERN is N006-7726. And this document is a record for admitting a criminal charge.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a record for admitted criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it's submitted on 9 July 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. It was submitted on the said date at the police station in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this is a complaint of a criminal charge against an unknown perpetrator for the criminal act of kidnapping. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. It is speaking about kidnapping by unknown perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, again, this complaint was accepted even though the perpetrator had not been identified. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it does not mean that any report would be -- any and every report would be on identified perpetrator. In many of the records on criminal reports you will note that the word "NN," unknown person, is used for the perpetrators. So there is nothing unusual about this one report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting it is unusual. I'm simply asking you: Is that what it says on the document, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, Mr. Prosecutor, this is what is written in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And as you testified just earlier on, even though the perpetrator is unknown at this point, the police still have a legal obligation to try to discover the identity of that perpetrator. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The identity of these perpetrators should be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you could turn to the page in front of that, N006-7725. And this is Official Note number 325. Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that it's dated 10 July 2001?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, 10th of July, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see from the subject that this is a conducted conversation with a certain individual?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Conversation with the given person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see from the name that this person appears to be a relative of the victim in this case?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the person who is reporting the event as we saw in the previous document. The report is made on the criminal -- a record is made on the criminal report filed and that the complainant is a relative of the abducted person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can we go forward two pages to N006-7727. This is an unnumbered Official Note. Do you have that document in front of you, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that it is headed: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, sector for interior Skopje"?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the subject is: Conducted official conversations with two persons who are named, kidnapped and maltreated by the Albanian terrorists. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And from the first line of the next paragraph, can you see that this conversation took place on the 28th of February, 2002?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, on the 28th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you could turn to the next page in the Macedonian version, Mr. Stojkov, and this is still on the same page in the English version. So it is 7728 in the Macedonian but remaining on the same page in English. Do you see the first paragraph in the Macedonian version and it's in the middle of the page in English starting: "Driving on the old road from Vratnica." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you carry on to the end of that paragraph, it says: "They were intercepted by four unknown uniformed and armed persons." And carrying on to the next paragraph it states: "The same were dressed in camouflage uniformed with NLA insignia on the sleeves of the uniforms." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I would like you now to turn forward three pages, two pages in the English. It will be NOO6-7730 in Macedonian and N006-7729 in English. And I'd like you to look at the first paragraph on the page that you're looking at, Mr. Stojkov, and it's midway down the page in the English page, and there's a paragraph starting: "While he was in the house." Do you follow that, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that it states: "While he was in the house, to Dragi was granted the request to write a letter to his family and the same was sent through the Red Cross from whom he received a letter from his wife." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you continue down approximately four paragraphs, do you see a paragraph starting: "After the short meeting ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it states: "After the short meeting between the terrorists and the International Red Cross, three named individuals were delivered to the persons from the ICRC and with their vehicles were taken to the positions of the Macedonian security forces, where they were finally released and met with their families." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it and I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So you can see that, according to this Official Note, in this situation, the NLA negotiated with representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is noted here that they had a meeting, the NLA and the International Red Cross, so they had contacts. And so I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in fact is says here, doesn't it, that these abducted persons were released to the ICRC by the NLA, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that these persons were freed by the International Red Cross. So with negotiations by the International Red Cross these persons were released by the NLA and taken over by the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you look at the bottom of the page and over to the next page in English, do you see your name listed as a submitter of this document?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. That is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would seek to tender this document 65 ter 1091 and I would also ask -- seek to tender the previous file which was 65 ter 1084.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's tab 5 and tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In that order, they will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1084 will become Exhibit P565, and 65 ter 1091 will become Exhibit P566.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you could please turn to tab 8, Mr. Stojkov. This is 65 ter number 1111. And we have the first page in Macedonian. We don't have a translation for that page in English. But do you recognise this as another file from your working group's documents?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you read for us what it says on the cover page, omitting any names that may be on there. And, again, I ask that this not be published.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no names. The title is: "Dossier, case file." Then there are lines left to note the full name, residence, Official Note, medical documents, photographic documents, and note.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please go to page 3 in the Macedonian version, page 2 in the English and this is N006-7915. And this is an unnumbered Official Note. Do you see that document?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see that this is an Official Note relating to an interview conducted with an individual and that document -- that interview took place on 17 October 2002. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Official Note, on interview conducted with such-and-such person in relation to a physical maltreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you go to the start of the second paragraph, the first line, do you see that it begins to describe an event that started on 18 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, then, that this Official Note was prepared over a year after the event in question and also well after the amnesty law had come into effect?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the date, it is possible that it was produced one year after the event, and certainly after the Law on Amnesty because the Law on Amnesty entered into force in March, if I remember correctly now. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you could turn to the next page which is N006-7916. Do you see your name at the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you could turn to the next page, do you see that this is a medical record obtained by the working group and it comes from the JZO clinic centre in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, yes. That is some document from the clinic centre in Skopje. That is a medical document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this file at this time, 65 ter 1111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P567, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you could turn next, Mr. Stojkov, to tab 10. And if you could turn to the second page in Macedonian, the first page in English. You will see that this is an Official Note. And can you see, Mr. Stojkov, that this is dated 10 October 2002. Do you see that? Sorry, Mr. Stojkov. I can see from here that it appears that you may be in the wrong tab. I'm looking in tab 10.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: It's fine. And do you see that this is an Official Note relating to an interview conducted with an individual in relation to his abduction by Albanian terrorists. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you look at the second paragraph, do you see that the incident that this Official Note relates to occurred on 23 July 2001?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So do you agree that we can see from this that work on this file continued well over a year after the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you turn to the last page, can you tell if you see your page -- sorry, your name at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my name and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to admit -- to tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P568, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkov, we have just one more file from the working group that I'll ask you to look at, and I'm sure you will be happy to hear that this will be the last one we'll go through. And this is in tab 11, 65 ter 1110. And do you see that this -- the first page has the heading: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, criminology techniques." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it states: "File, murder that took place on 5.5.2001," in the house of a named individual in Selce village when the owner was murdered. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojkov, from the name of that individual, are you able to tell whether that person was an ethnic Macedonian or ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ethnic Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if -- perhaps we could go through the next pages in Macedonian. They're feature photographs. We don't have English translations as such, so if we could just move through on to the next page. And do you see there, Mr. Stojkov, what appear to be photographs of a village?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could go to the page N006-7886. This should be the sixth page. And do you agree that what we can see here appears to be the interior of a house, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that there appears to be a person seated in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Does the appearance of the person in these photographs give you any indication of his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ethnic Albanian origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So you would agree that in this case, apparently, police were able to gain access to the interior of this person's house?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since photographs were made, they did have access in the village of Selce.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojkov, do you know where Selce village is?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been there personally. I know that it's under the Tetovo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you know whether this is a population which is largely ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the population is mixed. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true, Mr. Stojkov, that during the conflict in 2001, this village was perceived by the Macedonian authorities as being pro-NLA?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say how the villages were qualified because my work, at that period of time was altogether different. I carried out tasks given to me by my superiors. As for the qualification of villages, this went -- this was broadcast publicly through the media and this is the individual opinion of people. If you ask me, I know that the village of Sipkovica is the place and the centre where the NLA was located. As for other villages, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, was anything broadcast publicly through the media about the village of Selce and where its sympathies might lie?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot respond to this question. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. If we could please move on to the photograph which is page N006-7894. Do you have that page in front of you, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see what appear to be numbered markers in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what would such markers be used for?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the on-site investigations conducted by the forensics department that I participated in… these are used to mark the crime scene. However, I'm not an expert to say why these are used. As far as I know, these are markers to mark evidence at a crime scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can we move on to page N006-7895. And do you see, Mr. Stojkov, that this appears to be a photo of the victim in this case?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could now move to the page with the ERN N006-7902. And do you see there what appears to be a sketch of a crime scene, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see. This is, I regret to say, a sketch from a murder scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you agree that it appears a pretty thorough inspection was done of the crime scene here?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, again, this was done in an ethnic Albanian village. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I don't know whether this is exclusively an ethnic Albanian village. I cannot confirm this, because I have never been there and I don't know where it is. But the forensic inspection team went to the scene, and this is their investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, Mr. Stojkov. I do recall you saying you weren't aware of the -- the makeup of that village, but you are aware that this was at least the house of an ethnic Albanian. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, the house of is of an ethnic Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, can we please turn to page with the ERN N006-7911. This should be near the end, Mr. Stojkov. I believe it's page 31 in the Macedonian, and it's the fourth page in the English translations. Do you see, Mr. Stojkov, that this is an Official Note dated 6 May 2001, and it's an interview in relation to the death of this individual?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you please turn to the page before that, N006-7910. This is an Official Note dated 7 May 2001. And you see from this that this is an Official Note of another interview in relation to this incident.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And just looking towards the end of the paragraph, do you see where it states: "The murder of his father took place on 5.5.2001 at about 2200 hours and was committed by five armed persons dressed in uniforms and who spoke Albanian and Serbian." Do you see that? This should be at the bottom of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the start of the paragraph after that states: "On 5.5.2001 in the evening at about 2200 hours five armed individuals in black uniforms came into our home ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that individuals dressed in black uniforms and speaking Albanian would be an indication that these were NLA members?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All indications point to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you could please turn to the page in front of that, which is N006-7909. And you will see that this is a document headed: "Ministry of Interior SOI Tetovo." It is dated 8.5.2001. And then it says: "Basic public prosecutor, Tetovo." Carrying down a little bit it says: "Criminal charges." Do you see that, Mr. Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it states: "Criminal charges against unknown perpetrator for committing a crime, terrorism." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, in this case, an investigation was undertaken, interviews were done, the crime scene was extensively analysed and charges were filed. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here a criminal report is submitted against an unknown perpetrator. However, the case has not been fully resolved. However, it's true that a criminal report was submitted against an unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this was submitted to the basic public prosecutor in Tetovo, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So would you agree that simply because the identity of a perpetrator of a crime is unknown, that alone is not a valid reason to pass the case on to the public prosecutor for investigation, of charges, sorry?

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual practice in the Macedonian police is upon registering a criminal act perpetrated in which case the perpetrator cannot be immediately found and arrested, it is necessary to inform the public prosecutor's office and the courts about this criminal and legal incident. This report can be done immediately after the incident by the duty officers and criminal report is submitted against an unknown perpetrator to the public prosecution so as they can give further direction for further investigation of this criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, I left out a word in my question to you and I would just like to make that clear for the record. And my question should have been that simply because the identity of a perpetrator of a crime is not known, that alone is not a valid reason not to pass the case or pass the charges on to the public prosecutor. Is that correct? I'm sorry to ask to you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: IGNO STOJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All criminal and legal incidents for which there is evidence that they have been committed are reported to the public prosecutor's office. Is this -- if this is what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document, Your Honour, 65 ter 110.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Under seal, Your Honours, if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would ask that Exhibits P565 to P568 also be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we can manage to do that, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1110 will become Exhibit P569, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn, is that, then, a convenient time to end for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it would be, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're, as I indicated yesterday, experimenting a little with sitting times this week. We will adjourn for the night and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of February, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
